title: Separate PDF access from physical printing
description: Provide download and open actions for successful printable output while keeping both actions explicitly separate from physical printing and incapable of creating a physical-print assertion.
acceptanceCriteria: Download and open controls appear only for a complete successful generation with a durable print preparation
The actions are named as downloading or opening a PDF, never as confirming or completing printing
Using either action creates no physical-print event, printed status, stock usage, calibration evidence, or printer metadata
Visible copy states that PDF geometry is software evidence only and does not prove physical scale, placement, or printing
The preparation inspector labels output as uncalibrated and distinguishes preparation timestamp from any physical event
Controls and disclosures are keyboard operable, announced, and not color-dependent

steps.details: Define download and open as host-layer effects over successful PDF bytes and preparation identity, with no domain transition for printed, used, verified, or calibrated state.
Place persistent plain-language software-evidence and uncalibrated notices in Prepare PDF, success, download/open, and preparation-inspection states.
Create and revoke local object URLs safely, use a deterministic filename derived from non-secret project/preparation metadata, and expose separate semantic controls.
Show immutable snapshot identity, hash, layout revision/fingerprint, positions, timestamp, overrides, diagnostics, and uncalibrated status without a physical-print status field.
Use download and open controls in a browser, inspect durable state, and assert no physical-print, calibration, verification, stock-use, or printer assertion is created.

technicalNotes: The browser cannot inspect print-dialog choices or confirm that printing occurred.
Opening a PDF may invoke external software; that is still not evidence of physical output.
